subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should memory-core solve interrupted full reindexing with a validated resumable shadow generation, direct incremental writes to the live DB with incomplete-generation filtering, or defer checkpoint/resume support for now?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the repair changes durable memory generation semantics, incomplete-index search/status behavior, and possibly public memorySearch config, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Resumable shadow generation
options.body: Persist and validate generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB, resume compatible incomplete work, and publish only after the completed generation passes the current safety checks.

options.title: Direct live incremental writes
options.body: Write checkpointed progress into the live DB with explicit incomplete-generation status/search filtering, accepting a larger migration and compatibility surface.

options.title: Defer resume support
options.body: Keep the current safe full rebuild behavior and rely on embedding-cache reuse plus orphan cleanup until maintainers prioritize a broader memory indexing redesign.

recommendation.title: Resumable shadow generation
recommendation.body: Persist and validate generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB, resume compatible incomplete work, and publish only after the completed generation passes the current safety checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shadow publish semantics come from the database-first memory work he authored and reviewed, so he is the best available owner for the generation-contract choice.
